overall: Correctness: each of the 20 questions has exactly one defensible answer and none is ambiguous. In Parts 3 and 4 the correct options paraphrase the audio instead of repeating it ('boxes and labels' -> 'packing materials', 'lifts' -> 'elevators', 'send my assistant to collect them' -> 'have a staff member pick up the food'). Part 2 uses the real test's standard traps (Yes to wh-questions, answering a different question type, repeated words such as paper/working/client/kitchen, related words such as double-sided/double room), and qr-06, qr-07 and qr-08 are convincing indirect replies. However, five of the eight Part 2 items have direct, easy-to-spot answers, two of them starting with 'Yes', so the set is easier than real Part 2, which in my judgment relies more on indirect replies and also includes statements, choice questions and negative questions, none of which appear here. The Part 3 conversations are natural and work-based, with good traps (mixing up who did what in conv-03, 'noon' in conv-02) and the usual question types (topic, problem, next action, why a detail is mentioned), but they are shorter than real Part 3 conversations, have two questions instead of three, and include no three-speaker, graphic or quoted-phrase item. The Part 4 talks are typical genres (a building announcement and a voicemail) with good traps, but at five lines they are thinner than real Part 4 talks and would need more detail to support a third question; with no hard items overall (12 easy, 8 medium), the first priorities are indirect answers in Part 2 and longer scripts with a third question in Parts 3 and 4.
